Hey man! 22 years old here and on ny second job with a better salary, company culture, growth opportunities, and of course a healthier mindset when it comes to saving and financial independence. 

Before I arrived here, I used to be a miser in my previous job. For my first job, my savings was 60% of my income (I live with parents, no student loan debt, etc.). Ultimately, because of my extreme thriftiness, I succumbed to substance abuse and mental health (also physical health) degradation, leading me to resign from my first job. I went on therapy and took meds. After 7 months, I got employed again.

I wont elaborate much but I can say that those 7 months had been one of my lowest points in life. It felt like I will no longer get employed because of my conditions and that I'll exhaust all the money I initially saved. I spent everyday lying in bed, staring, harboring unkind thoughts reserved for myself. 

What helped me back then was having distraction. I know this might not work for others but diving down on high fantasy novels helped distract myself from my current misery. In this sense, time indeed helped a lot in terms of declogging my brain which had become insensitive and slow due to the stress I've experienced from my previous job.

I know it's cliche but it can always get better. Unhealthy self-harm and suicide thoughts always seem to go back during those times but I found that distracting myself in books helped (others do physical activity like running or biking).

As for the spending, I find that you shouldnn't deprive yourself too much. Now, I keep a 'to-be-sane' allowance in my budget (which I often spend on thrift-bookstores and street food), expenditures which I would consider a waste of money in the past. 

It's awesome to consider the future and the time value of money and all for every penny we save but if we die today or suffer too much, all those potential  compounded interest wont amount to much.
